skill.name: Next.js Better Auth Integration
skill.description: Guides conceptual Better Auth integration for Next.js App Router applications.
skill.summary: Plan secure Better Auth sessions, protected routes, and authentication flows in Next.js App Router.
skill.author: Claude

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. It labels a server-component session-access recommendation as network reconnaissance, but the skill contains no reconnaissance steps, requests, or executable code. No prompt injection, secret-exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use server components for server-side session access

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited text recommends server-side session access in Next.js server components. It contains no host discovery, port scanning, network request, or reconnaissance instruction.

content.value_statement: Setting up authentication across routes and components can be difficult. This skill provides a structured plan for Better Auth sessions, protected routes, and secure authentication practices.
actual_capabilities: Outlines Better Auth initialization requirements for a Next.js App Router application.
Explains session access patterns for server and client components.
Describes middleware-based protected routes and unauthorized redirects.
Covers JWT settings, token refresh, and secure token handling concepts.
Lists security, testing, error-handling, and performance considerations for authentication flows.
limitations: Provides conceptual guidance rather than installable code or configuration files.
Does not configure a database, identity provider, or environment variables.
Does not replace a security review of an application's authentication implementation.
Targets Next.js App Router and does not cover Pages Router integration.

use_cases.title: Plan a new application login
use_cases.description: Create an authentication integration plan before building a Next.js App Router application.

use_cases.title: Review protected route design
use_cases.description: Check middleware, session access, and redirect behavior for protected application pages.

use_cases.title: Prepare authentication tests
use_cases.description: Build a checklist for session persistence, token validation, and login failure scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Start an integration plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic Better Auth integration plan for my Next.js App Router application.

prompt_templates.title: Protect application pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Describe how to protect these App Router paths with middleware: /dashboard, /settings, and /billing.

prompt_templates.title: Review session handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed server and client session access design. Identify missing security controls and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Design a robust authentication flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Better Auth authentication plan with JWT expiration, refresh behavior, secure cookies, CSRF protection, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Plan protected routes for an App Router dashboard.
output: Identify the routes that require a valid session.
Use middleware to redirect unauthenticated visitors.
Verify the session again in server-side data access paths.
Test direct navigation, expired sessions, and return URLs.

output_examples.input: What should I secure in a Better Auth login flow?
output: Store session cookies with secure and HTTP-only attributes.
Validate authentication inputs and callback URLs.
Apply CSRF protection and rate limits to authentication endpoints.
Keep signing secrets in protected environment management.

best_practices: Keep authentication secrets outside source control and rotate them when exposure is suspected.
Authorize sensitive server actions independently of client session state.
Test successful, expired, revoked, and unauthorized session scenarios.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on client-side checks to protect sensitive data or actions.
Do not store long-lived session tokens in insecure browser storage.
Do not accept unvalidated redirect URLs or authentication callback inputs.

faq.question: Does this skill install Better Auth?
faq.answer: No. It provides conceptual implementation guidance and does not install packages or modify files.

faq.question: Which Next.js router does it support?
faq.answer: It targets the App Router architecture in Next.js 13 and later.

faq.question: Does it provide production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. Validate generated code against current Better Auth and Next.js documentation before deployment.

faq.question: Can it help protect routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains middleware, server-side checks, redirects, and testing considerations for protected routes.

faq.question: Does it manage authentication secrets?
faq.answer: No. You must configure secure secret storage and environment access in your own deployment environment.

faq.question: Does it replace an authentication security review?
faq.answer: No. Review your final implementation for authorization, session handling, input validation, and deployment-specific risks.
